text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The forum for Europisation of the Balkans due to be held at the end of the month in Macedonia has been postponed. All neighbours showed reserves towards the Macedonian initiative. Leaders of all Balkan countries and former U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali were to take part.
- Over 1,000 Macedonian students demonstrate in front of the Skopje rectorate against Albanian language classes at the Teachers' Academy demanding resignation of Education Minister Sofia Todorova.

- Macedonian students are instruments in the govenrment's hands which wants to create "false inter-ethnic tensions over minority issues," says ethnic Albanian PDPA party commenting student protests in Skopje on Tuesday.

- Special U.N. human rights rapporteur for the former Yugoslvaia Elisabeth Rehn is disappointed with the slow development of human rights in Macedonia. "Police harassment continues and the question of higher education in the Albannian language remains open," she said Tuesday evening in Skopje.
- The Confederation of Independent Trade unions in Macedonia appeals to all workers to make fresh efforts at organising their movement in order to secure more rights.
